summary.text: The quantile function of a probability distribution is the inverse of its cumulative distribution function, and it is also called the percentile function.
It is one way of prescribing a probability distribution, as an alternative to the density or mass function and the cumulative distribution function.
It gives key percentage points such as the median and quartiles, and in simulations it turns uniform random numbers into draws from other distributions.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Percentile function, percent-point function, inverse CDF

facts.label: Key points
facts.value: Used for the median, quartiles and 5% or 95% levels

facts.label: Sampling
facts.value: Applied to a uniform sample to sample another distribution

facts.label: Normal case
facts.value: Derived from the standard normal's probit function

facts.label: Finance and economics
facts.value: Its integral gives the Lorenz curve

items.prompt: A teacher says a distribution can only be specified by its density or mass function. What else can specify one?

options.label: Only the mean and the spread
The quantile function, among other functions
Only its highest point
Nothing else can

items.explain: The quantile function is one way of prescribing a probability distribution, an alternative to the density, mass and cumulative distribution functions.

items.prompt: A researcher needs the 2.5% and 97.5% cut-offs of a known distribution to judge whether an observation is significant. Which function gives them?

options.label: The probability density function
The probability mass function
The indicator function
The quantile function

items.explain: Quantile functions give key percentage points of a distribution, such as the 5%, 95%, 2.5% and 97.5% levels.

items.prompt: A computer can only draw numbers spread evenly between 0 and 1. How can it produce numbers from some other distribution?

options.label: Apply that distribution's quantile function to the uniform draws
Add up many of the uniform draws
Round each draw to the nearest whole number
Multiply each draw by the distribution's mean

items.explain: A sample from a given distribution can be obtained by applying its quantile function to a sample from a uniform distribution.

items.prompt: Statistics software lists a percent-point function for a distribution. Which other function is it the same as?

options.label: The probability mass function of the distribution
The Lorenz curve used in economics
The inverse of the cumulative distribution function
The density function of the distribution

items.explain: The percent-point function is another name for the quantile function, which is the inverse of the cumulative distribution function.

items.prompt: How can the quantile function for a normal distribution with any mean and spread be obtained?

options.label: By a simple transformation of the standard normal's quantile function
By solving a short algebra formula for each mean
By taking the derivative of the density
By rebuilding a fresh table for each mean

items.explain: The normal distribution is a location-scale family, so its quantile function for arbitrary parameters comes from a simple transformation of the standard normal quantile function, the probit function.

items.prompt: What is true about writing the probit function down as a formula?

options.label: It is a plain formula built from squares and roots
It has no closed form in basic algebra, so approximations are used
It is identical to the density function itself
It can only be found by reading off a printed table

items.explain: The probit function has no closed-form representation using basic algebraic functions, so approximate representations are usually used.
